items.stem: A classification prompt works in testing but occasionally obeys instructions hidden inside the user's message. What is the most direct mitigation?

options.text: Separate user content from instructions with delimiters and tell the model to treat delimited text as data, not commands
options.rationale: Correct: isolating untrusted input reduces instruction injection.
Output length does not address injection.
Few-shot vs zero-shot is unrelated to injection defence.
More randomness does not prevent obeying injected instructions.

items.explanation: Correct: isolating untrusted input reduces instruction injection.

items.stem: Which TWO practices make a production prompt maintainable like code? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Keeping the prompt under version control with a change history
options.rationale: Correct: versioning tracks changes and enables rollback.

options.text: Maintaining a regression test set run on every prompt change
options.rationale: Correct: tests catch quality regressions before release.

options.text: Editing the live prompt by hand whenever output looks wrong
options.rationale: Untracked hand-edits are exactly what to avoid.

options.text: Avoiding any examples because they take tokens
options.rationale: Dropping helpful examples to save tokens can hurt quality; it is not a maintainability practice.

items.explanation: Correct: versioning tracks changes and enables rollback.

items.stem: When is adding few-shot examples most likely to help?

options.text: When the desired output format or edge-case handling is hard to specify in words alone
options.rationale: Correct: examples convey format and edge cases that prose struggles to pin down.
Examples add cost and are not always needed.

options.text: Only when the temperature is zero
options.rationale: Few-shot usefulness is independent of temperature.

options.text: Never, because examples always reduce accuracy
options.rationale: Examples often improve accuracy for format-sensitive tasks.

items.explanation: Correct: examples convey format and edge cases that prose struggles to pin down.
